evals.name: clock-boundary
evals.prompt: tests/test_reports.py::test_report_timestamp fails maybe once every few CI runs but i can never get it to fail locally. can you figure out whats going on and fix it
evals.expected_output: Measures the flake (~15%), identifies that the report timestamp is taken before a slow load and compared with a second datetime.now() so it fails when a second boundary is crossed, fixes by freezing/injecting the clock or asserting a before/after range, and verifies with many clean reruns.

evals.name: order-dependent-polluter
evals.prompt: our CI keeps failing on tests/test_pricing.py::test_default_currency but when I run test_pricing.py by itself it passes every time. what's breaking it? please fix it properly, not a hack
evals.expected_output: Shows it passes alone and fails in some suite orders, identifies tests/test_admin.py::test_switch_store_to_euro as the polluter (sets settings.currency without restoring), fixes the polluter with monkeypatch (or equivalent cleanup), and verifies with shuffled suite runs.

evals.name: random-exposes-product-bug
evals.prompt: test_codes_are_unique in tests/test_coupons.py is flaky, fails like 1 in 5 runs. honestly I'm tempted to just slap @pytest.mark.flaky(reruns=3) on it and move on. can you sort it out?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the flake is a real bug: generate_codes can return duplicate codes (4-letter alphabet, length 2, no collision check). Fixes generate_codes to guarantee distinct codes (and handle impossible requests), does not add retries or seed the test, and verifies.

evals.name: not-actually-flaky
evals.prompt: tests/test_cart.py::test_cart_total failed once on CI yesterday and then passed when we re-ran the job. can you fix the flakiness in it?
evals.expected_output: Tries hard to reproduce (many isolated + shuffled runs, stress), finds no failures, explains what the numbers rule out and what to collect next time (CI log, env), and makes no code changes.

evals.name: buried-cache-polluter
evals.prompt: CI runs our suite with pytest-randomly and tests/test_checkout.py::test_order_total[standard] fails maybe every other run. running plain `pytest` locally it always passes. there are ~180 tests so idk where to even start. can you find whats causing it and fix it
evals.expected_output: Shows it is order-dependent, finds test_promotions.py::test_flash_sale_price[WID-100S-20] as the polluter among ~180 tests, identifies that flash_sale_price mutates the lru_cached catalog dict (a product bug), fixes the product code so prices aren't mutated, and verifies with shuffled runs.

evals.name: rare-float-set-order
evals.prompt: tests/test_invoices.py::test_invoice_total has failed maybe 3 or 4 times on CI in the last couple of months. nobody has ever reproduced it locally. worth looking into?
evals.expected_output: Reproduces the rare (~9%) failure with many reruns, explains that summing floats in set() iteration order (per-process hash randomisation) changes the last bits, fixes invoice_total to be deterministic and exact to the cent (sorted order and/or Decimal/rounding), verifies with ~200 clean runs.

evals.name: load-only-timing
evals.prompt: tests/test_ratelimit.py::test_blocks_fourth_call fails on CI every now and then (our runners are pretty overloaded tbh). never fails on my machine. can you fix it?
evals.expected_output: Reproduces it under CPU load (rare when idle), explains that ~5ms of signing per call against a 20ms real-time window races on slow machines, fixes deterministically (inject/fake the clock) rather than just widening the window, verifies under load.

evals.name: import-side-effect
evals.prompt: tests/test_refunds.py::test_refund_card_order passes when we run the whole suite but we just started sharding CI across 4 machines and it fails on some shards. please fix
evals.expected_output: Finds it fails whenever run without test_payments_card.py (import-time provider registration), recognises the product bug (refund_order can't find the card provider in production), fixes registration in product code, verifies it passes alone and in the suite.
